# kernel-profiles — first-class kernel profiles for limine

The ii shell used to carry a **static** `limine.conf` template that drifted
from the live `/boot/limine.conf`. Hand-editing the live file then broke real
boot entries (2026-09-17: `/CachyOS Main` lost its `cmdline` + initramfs, and a
stray duplicate `cmdline` block landed in the NVreg entry — both repaired).

Profiles fix this structurally: **edit data, not indentation.**

…

Changing the boot config now means editing a `.profile` file and running
`render.sh --install` — the renderer validates every linux entry (exactly one
`cmdline`, one `kernel_path`, ≥1 `module_path`, and every referenced
kernel/ucode/initramfs file present in `/boot`) and refuses to install a
broken config. The malformed-edit class of bug that broke `/CachyOS Main`
cannot pass validation.

`--check` is strict: `cmp -s` byte-for-byte against `/boot/limine.conf`.
Any drift — even a blank line — fails loudly with a unified diff.

Duplicate `cmdline` blocks are structurally impossible: the renderer emits
exactly one `cmdline:` line per entry via a single `printf` (by
construction), and any newline smuggled inside a profile field is a hard
render error (injection guard). `validate()` additionally asserts
`cmdline`/`kernel_path` appear exactly once per linux entry.

## Config-checksum enrollment (do not skip)

`/etc/default/limine` sets `ENABLE_ENROLL_LIMINE_CONFIG=yes`: the Limine
binary embeds a BLAKE2 checksum of `limine.conf`, and **an edit that is not
re-enrolled will not boot**. `render.sh --install` therefore runs
`limine-enroll-config` after the atomic rename, every time. Never hand-edit
`/boot/limine.conf` without re-enrolling afterwards.

## /etc/default/limine — single authoritative cmdline

This file is **live**, not dormant: it is consumed by `limine-entry-tool`
(`KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]` is applied to kernel entries on every kernel
install/update) and by `limine-common-functions` (enrollment, ESP path).
On 2026-09-18 it carried **two** `KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]` assignments;
bash last-wins meant the effective one was the *short* stock cmdline, so the
next kernel update would have silently regenerated entries *without* the
NVreg/amd_pstate/zswap tuning. Resolved: exactly one assignment — the full
tuned cmdline (matching `../default-limine`, which is the template). The
short duplicate is gone.
